facts.statement: A _headers file allows at most 100 rules and 2,000 characters per line
facts.quote: You may define up to 100 header rules. Each line in the `_headers` file has a 2,000 character limit.

facts.statement: A header applied by more than one matching rule is sent once with the values joined by a comma
facts.quote: If a header is applied twice in the `_headers` file, the values are joined with a comma separator.

facts.statement: A request that matches several rules inherits the headers of all of them
facts.quote: An incoming request which matches multiple rules' URL patterns will inherit all rules' headers.

facts.statement: The _headers file sits in the static asset directory and is not itself served
facts.quote: This file will not itself be served as a static asset, but will instead be parsed by Cloudflare Pages and its rules will be applied to static asset responses.

facts.statement: Custom headers are not applied to responses generated by Pages Functions

facts.statement: Redirects are applied before headers
facts.quote: redirects are applied before headers, so when a request matches both a redirect and a header, the redirect takes priority.

facts.statement: A header can be detached with "! " in front of its name
facts.quote: This can be done by prepending the header name with an exclamation mark and space (`! `).

facts.statement: HTML pages are served at their extension-less path; the .html form is redirected to it
facts.quote: Pages will also redirect HTML pages to their extension-less counterparts: for instance, `/contact.html` will be redirected to `/contact`, and `/about/index.html` will be redirected to `/about/`.

facts.statement: A custom 404 page is a 404.html file; the closest one up the directory tree is used
facts.quote: You can define a custom page to be displayed when Pages cannot find a requested file by creating a `404.html` file.

facts.statement: Without a top-level 404.html Pages assumes a single-page application
facts.quote: If your project does not include a top-level `404.html` file, Pages assumes that you are deploying a single-page application.

facts.statement: In that mode every path that is not a static asset is answered with the root
facts.quote: Pages' default single-page application behavior serves the root (`/`) for any incoming path that does not correspond to a static asset

facts.statement: Range requests are answered with 200, not 206
facts.quote: Pages currently returns `200` responses for HTTP range requests; however, the team is working on adding spec-compliant `206` partial responses.

facts.statement: Gzip and Brotli are served whenever possible
facts.quote: Pages will also serve Gzip and Brotli responses whenever possible.

facts.statement: A site may have 20,000 files on the free plan and 100,000 on paid plans, and 25 MiB per file

facts.statement: A _redirects file allows 2,000 static and 100 dynamic redirects

facts.statement: Preview deployments are public by default; Access protects previews only, not the pages.dev or custom domain
